item.title: Stark units and cyclotomic Iwasawa theory over complex cubic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.33349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For cyclotomic extensions of complex cubic fields, we prove the integral rank-$1$ and rational rank-$2$ abelian Stark conjectures. More generally, we prove a relative theorem on the higher-rank Rubin--Stark conjectures for cubic extensions of number fields. We then apply our Stark unit constructions to the Bergeron--Charollois--Garc\'{i}a conjectures on elliptic gamma values. Finally, we prove an Iwasawa main conjecture relating norm-compatible systems of Stark units to ideal class groups in cyclotomic towers over complex cubic fields.
item.dc:creator: Robin Zhang

item.title: Effective bounds for adjoint Bloch-Kato Selmer groups of Hilbert modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.33361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a totally real field and let $\Pi$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb A_F)$. Under the usual Taylor-Wiles residual irreducibility hypothesis, we prove the vanishing of the adjoint Bloch-Kato Selmer group with characteristic-zero coefficients and give an explicit upper bound for a corresponding Selmer group with divisible coefficients. The argument revisits Wiles's use of level raising at Taylor-Wiles primes. In place of freeness or almost freeness of automorphic cohomology over a Hecke algebra, we compare congruence modules at the original and auxiliary levels and control the part of the Hecke cotangent space detected by the automorphic module. This produces Galois cohomology classes with prescribed ramification at the auxiliary primes. The resulting bounds depend explicitly on congruence data at the original automorphic level and on torsion in cotangent spaces of local deformation rings.
item.dc:creator: Chandrashekhar B. Khare, Stefan Patrikis

item.title: Constructing Large Euler Pseudoprimes through Carmichael Products
item.description: arXiv:2611.33446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by recent work on Carmichael numbers and by the construction of Sanchez, et al., we revisit the subset product construction of Alford, et al. We state a theoretical parallel variant of the pushdown algorithm and extend computational records in two ways. First, we construct a Carmichael number that is an Euler pseudoprime to every base up to $1172819$, which includes the first $90968$ prime numbers. Second, we extend the known list of Carmichael numbers with exactly $d$ prime factors from $d \leq 19565220$ to $d \leq 340210163$.
item.dc:creator: Jon Grantham, Andrew Shallue, Jonathan Webster

item.title: Cartesian product of $\psi$-badly approximable sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.33553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we study the Cartesian products of sets in $\mathbb R^{d}$ that are $\psi$-approximable but not $c\psi$-approximable for arbitrarily small $c>0$, often denoted $\mathbf{Bad}_{d}(\psi)$. Setting $d=\sum_{i=1}^{N}d_i\in\mathbb N$ and $\psi_i(q)=q^{-\tau_i}$ with $\tau_i\geq 1/d_i$, $i=1,\ldots,N$, we calculate \[ \dim_{\mathrm H}\prod_{i=1}^{N}\mathbf{Bad}_{d_i}(\psi_i) =\min_{1\leq i\leq N}\left\{\frac{d_i+1}{\tau_i+1}+(d-d_i)\right\}=d- \max_{1\leq i\leq N}\left\{ d_i-\frac{d_i+1}{\tau_i+1} \right\}, \] for $\dim_{\mathrm H}$ denoting the Hausdorff dimension. The lower bound is obtained by combining the delayed-pruning construction of Koivusalo-Levesley-Ward-Zhang (IMRN, 2024) with the product Cantor-set method of Wang-Wu (TAMS, 2024).
item.dc:creator: Mumtaz Hussain, Johannes Schleischitz, Benjamin Ward

item.title: Symmetric identities and determinants for matrices composed of Legendre symbols
item.description: arXiv:2611.33667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove a series of identities and evaluate the determinants for a class of matrices composed of Legendre symbols given by Sun [10, Conjecture 3.2 (i)]. Together with [6] which proved Conjecture 3.2 (ii) in [10], these results provide a more general approach for a complete proof of Conjecture 3.2 in [10].
item.dc:creator: Roman Le Lan, Keqin Liu

item.title: Murmurations in Short Intervals for Elliptic Curves Ordered by Height
item.description: arXiv:2611.33781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Murmurations are the phenomenon, first observed by He, Lee, Oliver, and Pozdnyakov (2025), that the average value of $\epsilon(E) a_p(E)$, the $p$-th $L$-function coefficient weighted by the root number, over elliptic curves of conductor in some range $N(E) \in [N_1, N_2]$ seem to approximate a continuous, oscillating function. While murmurations have been proven for other families of $L$-functions (notably by Zubrilina (2025) for weight $k$ modular forms), the only unconditional murmuration formula for elliptic curves is a partial result by Sawin and Sutherland (2025) ordering by naive height instead of conductor. In this setting, murmurations appear by first averaging $\epsilon(E) a_p(E)$ for a single curve over $p \in (C_1, C_2)$ and then average over elliptic curves of bounded height. However, Sawin and Sutherland's results average $\epsilon(E) a_n(E)$ over all of $\mathbb{N}$ instead of a small interval $(C_1, C_2).$ In this work, we prove how small the interval $(C_1, C_2)$ can be taken while preserving the conclusion of Sawin and Sutherland's first murmuration formula (Proposition 7).
item.dc:creator: Aarya J. Kumar

item.title: Counting solutions to sparse systems of congruences
item.description: arXiv:2611.33927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain new bounds and asymptotic formulas for the number of solutions to sparse systems of $n$ diagonal congruences modulo an integer $q$ in $s$ variables. In a large range of parameters, our results improve and generalise those of A. A. Karatsuba (1976). In particular, our lower bound on $s$, which guarantees the solvability of such systems, depends only on $n$, rather than on specific degrees as in the work of A. A. Karatsuba (1976).
item.dc:creator: Subham Bhakta, Igor E. Shparlinski

item.title: $99.99\%$ of cubic surfaces have a rational point
item.description: arXiv:2611.33932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When cubic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ are ordered by height, we prove that almost every such surface satisfies the Hasse principle. This extends work of Browning, Le Boudec and Sawin and completes the proof of the conjecture of Poonen and Voloch for Fano hypersurfaces. We also obtain an upper bound for the least height of a rational point on almost all everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces and we give an upper bound for the number of cubic surfaces with a Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle. Finally, once combined with a calculation of Beneish and Keyes about the density of everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces, this establishes the explicit proportion of cubic surfaces that have a rational point.
item.dc:creator: Tim Browning, Anna Zanoli

item.title: Geometric realization of the local Langlands and local Jacquet-Langlands correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in a partially ramified case
item.description: arXiv:2611.34018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a new family of algebraic varieties over a finite field, realizing the local Langlands and local Jacquet-Langlands correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in their compactly supported \'etale cohomology. The resulting representations have $L$-parameters which are induced from characters of a partially ramified field extension.
item.dc:creator: Haruto Onishi

item.title: On pseudo-null Iwasawa modules, restricted ramification, and Non-freeness Conjecture over a quartic CM-field
item.description: arXiv:2611.34038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a CM-field of degree greater than $2$, $p$ an odd prime number that splits completely in $k$, and $\Sigma$ a $p$-adic CM-type of $k$. In this setting, we show the non-triviality of the $\Sigma$-ramified Iwasawa module of the maximal multiple $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension $\widetilde{k}/k$. As a consequence, under a weak form of Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture, we see that the unramified Iwasawa module and the $\Sigma$-ramified Iwasawa module of $\widetilde{k}$ never coincide. In the case where $k$ is a quartic CM-field, under a certain assumption, we show that the non-coincidence condition is equivalent to Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture. We also study a relation of the non-coincidence condition with Non-freeness Conjecture, which is a conjecture studied in non-abelian Iwasawa theory.
item.dc:creator: Takuya Yanagisawa

item.title: Simple ordinary geometrically split abelian varieties over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.33638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we provide a partial classification (necessary conditions) for all possible simple ordinary geometrically split abelian varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Let $A$ be such an abelian variety, i.e. $A$ is simple over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and splits as $A \sim B^s$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$ for some simple abelian variety $B$. Assume that $d$ is a minimal extension degree over which $A$ splits and $B$ has a minimal field of definition (up to isogeny) $\mathbb{F}_{q^e}\subseteq \mathbb{F}_{q^d}$. For dimension $2$, Howe and Zhu showed that the only possible degrees $d$ are $2$, $3$, $4$, and $6$. Moreover, for each such degree $d$, they provided explicit formulae expressing the isogeny invariant, namely the characteristic polynomial of the Frobenius endomorphism $\chi_{A,q}$, in terms of the coeffients of $\chi_{B,q}$. We extend this result to ordinary abelian varieties of higher dimension. For dimensions $3$--$10$, we provide complete lists of such varieties as components of the Weil restriction $W_{\mathbb{F}_{q^d}/\mathbb{F}_q}(B)$ together with all possible triples $(d, e, s)$ and restrictions on characteristic polynomial $\chi_{A,q}$ of the form $\chi_{A, q} \mid \chi_{V, q}$. Here, $V$ is a component of Weil restriction $W_{\mathbb{F}_{q^d}/\mathbb{F}_q}(B)$ containing $A$ as an isogeny factor and having explicit expression of the characteristic polynomial $\chi_{V,q}$ in terms of coefficients of $\chi_{B,q^e}$. For higher dimensions, we propose an algorithm for enumeration of all possible cases for a given dimension of $A$. We also provide an implementation of this algorithm.
item.dc:creator: S. A. Novoselov

item.title: Sections and Constant Fields of Postcritically Finite Rational Maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.33780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We relate the constant fields of generic preimage towers to two invariants of geometric monodromy. Bounded section indices characterize branching of the closed action and imply a finite constant extension. Unbounded finite-level abelianization orders force an infinite cyclotomic subextension. For a quadratic rational map with hyperbolic orbifold, we compute the section indices and abelianizations at every sufficiently large level and obtain an infinite real cyclotomic subextension. We also give a branching criterion for quadratic maps with neither critical point periodic and formulate three conjectures about the discrete action, the constants, and the case of bounded abelianizations with unbounded section indices.
item.dc:creator: Wayne Peng

item.title: The Brauer--Manin obstruction to weak approximation on a constant K3 surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.33908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a constant supersingular K3 surface over every global field of characteristic two for which rational points are Zariski dense but are not dense in the Brauer--Manin set. This shows that the analogue of Skorobogatov's conjecture over global function fields does not hold for supersingular K3 surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Valloni

item.title: Convolutions of Goss and Pellarin $L$-series
item.description: arXiv:2206.14931v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish special value results of convolutions of Goss and Pellarin $L$-series attached to Drinfeld modules that take values in Tate algebras. Applying the class module formula of Demeslay to certain rigid analytic twists of one Drinfeld module by another, we extend the special value formula for the Pellarin $L$-function associated to the Carlitz module and the Anderson-Thakur function to Drinfeld modules of arbitrary rank and their rigid analytic trivializations. By way of the theory of Schur polynomials these identities take the form of specializations of convolutions of Rankin-Selberg type. These convolution $L$-series are also identified with covolumes of Stark units.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Cheng Huang, Matthew A. Papanikolas

item.title: Transfer principles for Galois cohomology and Serre's conjecture II
item.description: arXiv:2308.00903v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we prove several transfer principles for the cohomological dimension of fields. Given a fixed field $K$ with finite cohomological dimension $\delta$, the two main ones allow to: - construct totally ramified extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq \delta - 1$ when $K$ is a complete discrete valuation field; - construct algebraic extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq \delta-1$ and satisfying a norm condition. We then apply these results to Serre's conjecture II and to some variants for fields of any cohomological dimension that are inspired by conjectures of Kato and Kuzumaki. In particular, we prove that Serre's conjecture II for characteristic $0$ fields implies Serre's conjecture II for positive characteristic fields.
item.dc:creator: Diego Izquierdo, Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche

item.title: Heights of Drinfeld modular polynomials and Hecke images
item.description: arXiv:2410.11132v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain explicit upper and lower bounds on the size of the coefficients of the Drinfeld modular polynomials $\Phi_N$ for any monic $N\in\mathbb{F}_q[t]$. These polynomials vanish at pairs of $j$-invariants of Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$-modules of rank 2 linked by cyclic isogenies of degree $N$. The main term in both bounds is asymptotically optimal as $\mathrm{deg}(N)$ tends to infinity. We also obtain precise estimates on the Weil height and Taguchi height of Hecke images of Drinfeld modules of rank 2.
item.dc:creator: Florian Breuer, Fabien Pazuki, Zhenlin Ran

item.title: An algorithm to compute upper bounds of dimensions for Siegel Modular Forms of Prime Level and Arbitrary Nebentypus
item.description: arXiv:2511.22207v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe an algorithmic method to determine the image of restriction maps for Siegel modular forms with \textit{arbitrary} characters and arbitrary weight. A program has been implemented in the mathematical software \texttt{Java} to compute the Fourier expansion of the image of these restriction maps for Siegel modular forms of genus two. This approach allows us to compute an upper bound for the space of Siegel modular forms with {\it non-trivial} character (which has not been previously known) and arbitrary weights (including low weight $k \leq 4$).
item.dc:creator: Debargha Banerjee, Dron Airon, Pranjal Vishwakarma, Ronit Debnath

item.title: Local square mean in the hyperbolic circle problem and sums of Sali\'e sums
item.description: arXiv:2604.11205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gamma \subseteq \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ be a finite volume Fuchsian group. The hyperbolic circle problem is the estimation of the number of elements of the $\Gamma$-orbit of $z$ in a hyperbolic circle around $w$ of radius $R$, where $z$ and $w$ are given points of the upper half plane and $R$ is a large number. An estimate with error term $e^{\frac 23R}$ is known. Recently, taking $z=w$ and considering $\Gamma = \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, we have shown the estimate $e^{\left(\frac 9{14}+\epsilon\right)R}$ for the local $L^2$-norm of the error term, which is better than the pointwise bound. Here we improve the exponent $\frac 9{14}$, conditionally on a twisted Linnik-Selberg-type conjecture for sums of Sali\'e sums.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'as Bir\'o

item.title: The arithmetic of critical values II: critical elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2608.29836v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this second chapter of the \textit{Arithmetic of critical values} series (ACV), we study certain double covers $E_f\to\mathbb{P}^1$ whose branch locus coincides with that of a quartic polynomial $f$. We give a direct proof of the fact, already shown non-constructively in ACV I, that the elliptic curves $E_f$ admit a $3$-isogeny. Our methods lead us to examine the Galois closure of $f:\mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$, whose rich geometry yields a congruence between $E_f$ and a second elliptic curve $E'_f$. We study their arithmetic and show that they are linked by a Selmer companionship for infinitely many $f\in\mathbb{Z}[X]$, allowing us to exhibit elements in certain Tate-Shafarevich groups which are visible in an abelian surface. We also give some dynamical and Diophantine applications of our constructions, as well as new examples of Jacobians isogenous to a power of an elliptic curve.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Naccarato

item.title: Multiple Zeta Values in Positive Characteristic: A Kaneko-Zagier-Type Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.37450v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study a comparison between $\infty$-adic and finite multiple zeta values in positive characteristic. We construct a surjective comparison map from the algebra of $\infty$-adic multiple zeta values to a quotient of the algebra of finite multiple zeta values. This map factors through the quotient by $\zeta_A(q-1)$, thereby establishing the well-definedness of a Kaneko-Zagier-type conjectural map. We further show that the comparison map is compatible with special values of Carlitz multiple polylogarithms, as well as with the corresponding $\star$-inverse values. As an application, we prove the upper bound predicted by Shi's dimension conjecture for finite multiple zeta values.
item.dc:creator: Hung-Chun Tsui

item.title: Graded Structures of $v$-adic Carlitz Multiple Polylogarithms and $v$-adic Multiple Zeta Values
item.description: arXiv:2610.25063v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms and $v$-adic multiple zeta values. We prove that, for every finite place $v$ of $\mathbb{F}_q(\theta)$, the natural weight gives a graded structure on the algebras generated by these values. Moreover, we show that every $\overline{\mathbb{F}_q(\theta)}$-linear relation among these values arises from an $\mathbb{F}_q(\theta)$-linear relation. In particular, our results establish a function field analogue of the Furusho-Yamashita direct sum conjecture and extend Chen's work from finite places of degree one to arbitrary finite places.
item.dc:creator: Hung-Chun Tsui

item.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2611.28178v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous \'etale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, where $\Omega_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor. In this note, using the Dwyer-Greenlees equivalence between $\ell$-completed objects and $\ell$-torsion objects, we prove that $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, and consequently, based on Kahn's early work, the Tate conjecture at positive characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Yunhao Sun

item.title: Arithmetic Winding Curves in $\mathbb{F}_1$ Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.30682v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two. Valuation covers carry these periods on the curve $Y_K$. Their normal coordinates realize deck shifts as Schwartz operators in Meyer's arithmetic trace formula, and their puncture differentials give the finite Euler factors of $\zeta_K$. We construct a sheaf on $Y_K$ for which the middle Fourier--Poisson representation embeds as a $C_K$-module in ordinary first sheaf cohomology. The Dedekind-zeta component is an equivariant direct summand. The injection uses valuation monodromy at the finite places and adelic Poisson summation on the archimedean charts. The cup product of two image classes vanishes with tensor-product coefficients, also after conjugating one factor. On the section side, tensor degree and integral jets give multiplicative lattices, explicit duality quotients, and relative theta identities. A principal cyclotomic twist with determinant one on truncated jets yields a quadratic lower bound for the logarithmic index in a family of increasing rank. The fixed-weight Poisson quotients preserve finite collections of Mellin derivatives at Hecke zeros of orders below their respective multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: SeungJu Lee

item.title: Dobrowolski-type lower bounds for canonical heights of polynomials of Frobenius type
item.description: arXiv:2611.32713v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and let $f\in\OK[x]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $d=p^r$ with $f\equiv x^d+c\pmod p$, such as $x^2+c$. We prove that every $\alpha\in\Kbar$ of degree $D$ over $K$ with infinite orbit under $f$ satisfies $$\hh_f(\alpha)\ \ge\ \frac{c_1}{D\log3D}\exp\bigl(-c_2\sqrt{\log3D}\bigr),$$ where $c_1,c_2>0$ depend only on $f$ and $K$. This implies $\hh_f(\alpha)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$, making progress towards the dynamical Lehmer conjecture. The polynomial $f$ need not be postcritically finite. For such polynomials, for instance $x^2+1$, no lower bound of polynomial decay in $D$ was previously known. For postcritically finite polynomials such as $x^2-1$, it improves the recent quadratic bound of Habegger and Schmidt. The method is motivated by Dobrowolski's proof on Lehmer's problem.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Mello

item.title: An elliptic Lehmer bound of exponent one at a supersingular prime
item.description: arXiv:2611.32749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with good supersingular reduction at a prime $\p$. We prove that the N\'eron--Tate height of every non-torsion $P\in E(\Kbar)$ satisfies $\hh_E(P)\ge c\,D^{-1}(\log3D)^{-1}\exp(-c'\sqrt{\log3D})$, where $D=[K(x(P)):K]$ and $c,c'>0$ depend only on $E$, $K$ and $\p$; so $\hh_E(P)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$. By a result of Elkies this applies to every elliptic curve over $\QQ$, and it improves the exponents of Masser and of Hindry and Silverman.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Mello

item.title: Conics and rational points of bounded height on cubic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2601.10895v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct auxiliary intersections covering points of bounded height on geometrically integral non-ruled cubic surfaces over a fixed number field, and prove uniform bounds for the contribution of their conic components to rational and integral point counts. In the affine case, when the section at infinity is geometrically integral, the conic contribution admits a bound with a height exponent strictly below one. Under these hypotheses and within the same covering, obtaining a uniform bound for all integral points with any exponent greater than one reduces to controlling components of degree at least three. The proof combines a form of the global determinant method that retains the dependence on the height of Cayley form with uniform estimates for the number of conics of bounded height. The Deligne pairing and the geometry of residual conic pencils yield cubic image curves in fixed coefficient spaces. Uniform point estimates on these curves control the distribution of conic heights, with constants independent of the surface and the pencil.
item.dc:creator: Chunhui Liu

item.title: Certified Return-Word Induction for a Perturbed Hofstadter Recursion: Global well-definedness, local frequencies and nonautomaticity
item.description: arXiv:2603.29622v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the parity-perturbed Hofstadter recursion $Q(1)=Q(2)=1$, $Q(n)=Q(n-Q(n-1))+Q(n-Q(n-2))+(-1)^n$. We give a computer-assisted proof of global well-definedness using 13 return words, 92 synchronized states and 122 two-source rules. An induction on the rank words identifies the four ordered physical source projections at every level. The marked word construction and a finite lag certificate then identify its binary output with the step word $s_j=(Q(j+1)-Q(j-1))/2$ of the recursion. We determine the frequency of $001100$ in prefixes of $s$ as a function of the position within each pair of epochs. After rescaling the prefix length by $4^m/3$, the frequency converges uniformly to an explicit profile. Its minimum $1/96$ and maximum $1/48$ are the exact lower and upper limiting frequencies, and every value between them is a subsequential limit. The longest alternating factor among the first $N$ steps has length $2\log_2 N+O(1)$. It follows from Cobham's gap theorem that neither the step word nor $Q\bmod 4$ is automatic in any integer base $k\ge 2$.
item.dc:creator: Marco Mantovanelli

item.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16760v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the structure of \'etale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over rings of integers of number fields. We show that the image of the geometric \'etale fundamental group is FAb, while the kernel of the map to the fundamental group of the base need not be FAb or finitely generated. Our results rely on finiteness theorems for Galois coinvariants of geometric \'etale fundamental groups and \'etale cohomology over finitely generated fields. These apply to Galois extensions $L/k$ for which $\mathrm{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As a further application, we establish finiteness of prime-to-characteristic $L$-rational torsion on abelian varieties over $k$.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Steklov

item.title: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.19749v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is the evaluation of its theta series at a real nome and is relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The ratio of the Gaussian mass of stable lattices to the Gaussian mass of the integer lattice was conjectured to be $\le 1$ (Regev et al., 2024). Kominers proved this bound recently for lattices obtained by Construction~A from binary self-dual codes. Building on Kominers' bound, we establish corresponding inequalities on average for Construction~$A_4$ lattices obtained from free self-dual quaternary codes and for Construction~$A_6$ lattices obtained from self-dual senary codes. We also prove the strict Gaussian-mass inequality for extremal unimodular lattices of both Type~II and Type~I. The Type~I result uses the Rains--Sloane definition of extremality. Its proof combines a universal theta truncation with an exact inversion of the shadow coefficients, and a Gaussian inequality for translated lattices. In addition, we obtain an averaging bound over the genus of Type~II lattices, and extend the binary Construction~A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under conditions on the residue code.
item.dc:creator: Minjia Shi, Xinguang Dai, Patrick Sol\'e
